# M9: Polish and review

**Model:** Opus 5.5, high. **Paste to start:** `Read CLAUDE.md, then docs/build/STATUS.md and docs/build/scenes/M9.md, and do M9. Stop for my review at the end.`
**Spec:** `sed -n 491,545p PROTEST_VIZ_SPEC.md` (cross-cutting requirements, milestones and QA). Shared rules: [README.md](README.md).

## Purpose
Make the whole piece robust: an architect review and a GPU/performance review (Vali's usual process: Sonnet research/review agents, ask Vali for model and effort), accessibility, reduced motion, four viewports, and the promotion of v3 to `/index.html` (D1).

## Allowed data keys
None new. Check, don't add: every on-screen string still traces to `data/story/*.json` (or the D11 corpus for S7).

## Files it owns
- Fixes anywhere, **each with Vali's OK** (this is the one chat allowed to touch the shell and shared modules), logged in STATUS.
- D1 promotion at the end, only when Vali says: move v2 `index.html` → `archive/index-v2-fieldfile.html`, v3 → `index.html`. **Pushing to `main` deploys to Vercel**: never push without Vali.

## Must not touch
`data/story/*` (facts are F1's), `src/roach/roach.js` (verbatim), the storyboard frames.

## Contracts it consumes
All of STATUS "Contracts in force". Tools: `tools/cdp-scroll.mjs`, `tools/compare.mjs`, `tools/qa-shell.mjs`.

## Key frames
Every `docs/build/scenes/targets/*.json`, at 1280×720, 1440×900, 1920×1080 and 2560×1440 (`SIZE=w,h`), down and up.

## Done when
- `prefers-reduced-motion`: static swarm composition, static scenes, charts in final state, the keyword still works (crossfade instead of collapse). The controller has no global reduced-motion switch yet: add one (e.g. `ctx.reduced`) with Vali's OK.
- Performance: 60 fps at 1440×900 on an M-series Mac; every loop pauses off-screen (the controller only ticks live scenes; check nothing else runs a rAF); DPR ≤ 2; roach-count guard (20 ms for 2 s → −15%).
- Accessibility: keyboard path through the keyword, scrubber and CTA; visible focus; alt text from captions; AA contrast over the halftone.
- Robustness: no console errors or warnings; no runtime network calls except reader-started YouTube. **anime.js still loads from the jsDelivr CDN** (F3 kept v2's import-map pattern): self-host it under `static/vendor/` (same version, no new dependency) to meet spec §8.
- `qa-shell` all PASS at every viewport; review agents' findings fixed or logged.
